summary.value: The Pedres Portuguesa is a traditional farm chicken from Portugal and one of the country's four native breeds. It is found across mainland Portugal but is most common in the northwest, and its home area is the old province of Minho and nearby parts of Douro Litoral and Tras-os-Montes. It comes in just one pattern: fine dark gray bars on a white or pale gray background, which gives the breed its name. The single comb has five or six points, the face and earlobes are bright red, and the bare shanks are pale yellow marked with slate. Roosters weigh about 5.7 to 7 pounds and hens about 4.9 to 6 pounds. Birds are active, resist disease and do well on free range, and they are raised for both meat and eggs. Anglers also use the barred feathers to tie trout flies.
